candidates.title: Compute formalizable lifecycle consequences outside the model
candidates.rule: When dynamically removing or reconfiguring harness components, use explicit dependency and cleanup semantics to compute or verify consequences where those effects can be modeled.
candidates.passage: the finite semantics solves the controlled instances exactly.
candidates.finding: The finite reference semantics agrees with the controlled runtime observations, while models make target, minimality and final-state errors. The recommendation to place this checker in a harness is inferred; a complete deployed-agent comparison is not shown.
candidates.conditions: Dependencies and effect structure must be represented faithfully. Formal and Cordis-native tasks have different schedule coverage.
candidates.limitations: Restricted cleanup behavior excludes irreversible effects, hot replacement and failures. Large interaction counts are stress tests. Exactness inside the model does not imply the specification captures every real runtime effect.
candidates.validation_test: Compare model-only and reference-checked reconfiguration in a disposable runtime; verify target attainment, minimality and all relevant teardown orders, then test unmodeled effects separately.
